Theme

School & learning

author noun

also writer, writers, authors

classical

Liv. praef. 3: in tantā scrīptōrum turbā
Sall. Cat. 8.3: scrīptōrum magna ingenia
Traupman 170, 275, 409

scrīptor, scrīptōris m.

noun, third declension

a writer, an author

One who composes in writing, the word’s ruling sense (Lewis & Short); with a genitive, the author of a kind of work: rērum scrīptōrēs, historians (Liv. 21.1.1). Traupman gives scrīptrīx for a woman writer (p. 170).

Other words

  • auctor, auctōris m./f. — the author of a work; an authority one reads and cites

    noun, third declension, masculine or feminine · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.18.1: quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs; Suet. Jul. 56: Bellī Alexandrīnī Āfricīque et Hispāniēnsis incertus auctor est (Lewis & Short); Traupman 275

    The one a work comes from, and so one whose word counts; also the author of a plan or a deed. Lewis & Short makes it common gender; Traupman’s auctrīx (p. 275) is rare and post-classical (Lewis & Short s.v. auctrīx).

Examples

  • et sī in tantā scrīptōrum turbā mea fāma in obscūrō sit, nōbilitāte ac magnitūdine eōrum mē, quī nōminī officient meō, cōnsōler

    and if, in so great a crowd of writers, my own fame should stay in the shade, I shall console myself with the distinction and greatness of those who will eclipse my nameLiv. praef. 3

  • habeō nōn nūllōs ex iīs quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs quī dīcant fierī id oportēre

    I have several among the authors I am reading now who say that this ought to be doneCic. Att. 12.18.1

See also book, write, article, library.
